faqs.question: What is GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)?
faqs.answer: GEO is the practice of optimizing your website so that AI-powered search engines — including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and Gemini — can discover, understand, and cite your content. Unlike traditional SEO, which optimizes for ranked lists of blue links, GEO optimizes for being selected as a cited source in AI-generated answers. The core pillars are: (1) AI crawler access (robots.txt allowing GPTBot, ClaudeBot, etc.), (2) machine-readable content (llms.txt, JSON-LD schema), and (3) authority signals (E-E-A-T).

faqs.question: How is GEO different from SEO?
faqs.answer: SEO optimizes for ranked lists of blue links on search engines like Google and Bing. GEO optimizes for being cited as a source in AI-generated answers. They overlap heavily — good content, structured data, and authority help both — but GEO requires explicit AI-crawler allowance in robots.txt, an llms.txt file, and machine-parseable schema for AI models. In practice, GEO is a superset of SEO that adds AI-specific requirements.

faqs.question: What is llms.txt?
faqs.answer: llms.txt is a markdown file placed at the root of your website (yoursite.com/llms.txt) that provides AI models with a curated summary of your site: what it is, who it serves, and which pages matter most. It is the machine-readable equivalent of an About page, designed to be ingested by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and other LLM-powered crawlers in a single fetch. It is a proposed standard (llmstxt.org) that emerged in 2024-2025.

faqs.question: How does GeoScore work?
faqs.answer: GeoScore audits any public URL across 11 weighted dimensions of GEO readiness (AI crawlability, AI guidance / llms.txt, structured data, meta and social tags, content quality, E-E-A-T signals, brand entity, citation readiness, discovery endpoints, agent-friendliness, and freshness), plus negative signals and prompt injection safety deductions. It produces a 0-100 score, radar chart, and prioritized fix files across Single URL, Batch Sitemap, and Compare Sites modes. Single browser audits are free; optional Pro monitoring uses a Cloudflare Worker and D1. The source code is MIT-licensed and available on GitHub.

faqs.question: Is GeoScore free?
faqs.answer: Single browser audits, the Chrome MV3 Extension, the CLI (npx geoscore <url>), and the MCP Server (geoscore-mcp) are free and open-source under the MIT license. Optional Pro, Studio, and Agency plans starting at $9/month add automated monitoring, cloud history, regression alerts, and PDF export, and a one-time $49 Fix Pack offers done-for-you implementation.

faqs.question: Which AI crawlers should I allow in robots.txt?
faqs.answer: At minimum, allow: GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot (OpenAI/ChatGPT), ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai (Anthropic/Claude), PerplexityBot (Perplexity), Google-Extended (Google Gemini and AI Overviews), and CCBot (Common Crawl, used by many models). GeoScore checks 20 AI crawlers, tells you which ones are blocked, and generates a copy-pasteable robots.txt snippet.

faqs.question: How do GeoScore live SVG score badges work?
faqs.answer: Point any Markdown or HTML image tag at https://geoscore.help/badge/yourdomain.com. A Cloudflare Pages edge function validates the public domain (with SSRF and private-IP protection), audits the site, caches the SVG badge for 6 hours, and color-codes your 0-100 score across four tiers (86+ green, 68+ blue, 36+ amber, under 36 red).

faqs.question: What does GeoScore Chrome Extension v1.9.0 add?
faqs.answer: GeoScore Chrome Extension v1.9.0 audits any active tab directly in Chrome's Side Panel, bypassing Cloudflare WAF challenges and supporting private localhost or staging apps. It compares raw SSR HTML against browser-rendered CSR DOM, automatically detects Shopify, WordPress, and Next.js tech stacks with tailored deployment instructions, inspects all 6 discovery endpoints in the background toolbar badge, and generates one-click Markdown/HTML live SVG badge snippets.

faqs.question: Does GeoScore include guides for Shopify, WordPress, and Next.js?
faqs.answer: Yes. GeoScore provides dedicated playbooks at /geo-for/shopify/, /geo-for/wordpress/, and /geo-for/nextjs/ (available in English and Chinese), plus a 4-tab deployment guide (Static HTML, Next.js, WordPress, Shopify) inside the Fix Files panel.

faqs.question: What is E-E-A-T and why does it matter for GEO?
faqs.answer: E-E-A-T stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness. Originally a Google Search Quality Rater guideline, it has become a key signal for AI models evaluating whether to cite a source. E-E-A-T is signaled by: author bylines with credentials, About/team pages, third-party reviews and citations, .edu/.gov inbound links, HTTPS, and transparent contact/ownership information. AI models prefer to cite sources that demonstrate real expertise.

faqs.question: Which AI search engines should I optimize for?
faqs.answer: As of 2026, the major AI search engines to optimize for are: ChatGPT (SearchGPT), Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, and domestic engines such as Kimi, Doubao, and Metaso. Each uses specific crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, ClaudeBot, DeepSeekBot, Bytespider, etc.) and structured-data signals. GeoScore audits across all of them.
